quoteFollowUp.notOpenedBody:
Hello,

I sent you quote {quoteNumber} {days} days ago and I am not sure it arrived — sometimes these end up filed away by the mail system.

Would you let me know either way? I am happy to send it again.

Best regards
quoteFollowUp.noAnswerWhy: They have read it, so repeating the quote adds nothing. The draft offers to talk it through.
quoteFollowUp.noAnswerBody:
Hello,

I wanted to check whether you had any questions about quote {quoteNumber}.

If something in it does not fit, tell me what and I will look at it with you — it is easier to talk through than to write.

Best regards
quoteFollowUp.expiringWhy: The deadline is the fact the customer cannot see and you can, so it comes before how long they have been quiet.
quoteFollowUp.expiringBody:
Hello,

A quick note that quote {quoteNumber} is valid for another {days} days.

If you would like to go ahead, let me know and I will get it started. If you need more time, that is no problem — say so and I will extend it.

Best regards
quoteFollowUp.expiredWhy: It has lapsed. Saying so, and offering a fresh one, is better than letting it go quiet.
quoteFollowUp.expiredSubject: Quote {quoteNumber} has expired — shall I renew it?
quoteFollowUp.expiredBody:
Hello,

Quote {quoteNumber} expired {days} days ago.

If it is still of interest I will happily issue an updated one — prices may have moved, so it is worth redoing properly rather than extending the old date.

Best regards

gettingStarted.title: Getting started
gettingStarted.subtitle: Welcome to Flux CRM
gettingStarted.description: Flux CRM is your central platform for managing the entire sales cycle: from the first contact with prospective customers, through to closing sales and after-sales support.

t01.q: How do I get started after signing in for the first time?
t01.a: After signing in you land on the CRM Dashboard, your home screen. It gives you a real-time summary of active leads, open deals, tasks falling due and assigned tickets. We recommend starting by creating your first Leads, then building the Pipeline with your sales opportunities.

t02.q: What does a typical sales flow look like?
t02.a: The standard path is: Lead → Contact + Company → Deal (Pipeline) → Quote → Order. A lead who shows interest is converted into a qualified contact, a deal is opened in the pipeline, a quote is sent and, once accepted, the order is generated.

t03.q: How do the lists work (contacts, leads, companies, quotes, orders, products)?
t03.a: Each list loads one page of rows at a time, 50 by default. Above the table you will find the search box, how many rows you are seeing out of the total, the selector to switch to 25, 50, 100 or 200 rows per page, and the arrows to move between pages. Search and filters work on the whole list, not just the page on screen, so searching for a customer finds them even if they are on page twenty. Search, filters, sorting and page all end up in the page address: you can copy it and send it to a colleague, bookmark it, and the browser's back button works as you would expect.

t04.q: How does navigation work?
t04.a: The sidebar groups everything into seven sections: Work (dashboard, calendar, tasks, chat), Customers (contacts, companies, leads), Sales (pipeline with targets, funnel, win/loss, forecasts and reports, then quotes, orders, products and finance), Support (overview, tickets, SLA, macros), Marketing and automation, Analytics, and Administration (users, roles, settings). Some items only appear if your plan includes the corresponding module. On a phone the sidebar gives way to a tab bar at the bottom with the most used sections.

t05.a: Yes. From the header at the top right you can change the theme (light/dark), the language (Italian/English) and the display currency. You can also change the sidebar layout and enable the sticky navbar through the layout controls.

quickAccess.title: Search and quick access
quickAccess.subtitle: Ctrl+K, quick create, recents
quickAccess.description: One field to reach any record without knowing which list it is in, a menu to create a new one from wherever you are, and the list of what you opened recently.

t01.q: How do I find a record quickly?
t01.a: Press Ctrl+K (⌘K on a Mac) from any screen; Ctrl+J works too, and there is a 'Search' button in the header for anyone who prefers the mouse. Type at least two letters and results come in as you type: up and down arrows to move, Enter to open, Esc to close. The tabs at the top of the panel narrow the search to one group — customers, sales, documents, support, work, marketing — and only appear if you have access to more than one. Besides records the search also understands commands: typing 'new contact' takes you straight to creating one.

t02.q: What does the search look through?
t02.a:
Leads, contacts and companies (name, email, phone, VAT number), deals, products and price lists, quotes, orders, contracts, invoices and credit notes (document number and customer name), tickets, tasks, appointments, campaigns, sequences, email templates, and attached documents, searched by file name. A phone number is found by typing at least four of its digits. It shows at most five results per type, and matches on text contained in the field: a name with a typo in it is not found.
You only see what you could already see: types excluded by your role or by the workspace's plan do not appear at all. Products and templates have no page of their own, so the result opens their list already filtered; a document opens the record it is attached to; a credit note opens its invoice.

t03.q: How do I create something without hunting for the right page?
t03.a: Use 'Quick create', the button at the top of the sidebar: it lists everything you are allowed to create — lead, contact, company, deal, product, price list, quote, order, contract, invoice, ticket, task, appointment, campaign, sequence — and opens the create form on the right screen. The list is filtered by your permissions and by the plan, so it only holds things you can really create; if there are none, the menu says so instead of opening empty. The same entries appear in the search panel when you open it without typing anything.

t04.q: What is the recents list for?
t04.a:
For going back to what you were looking at. The circular-arrow icon in the header opens the records you opened recently, grouped by type, with how long ago; the same ones appear on the left of the search panel before you type. It fills in on its own when you open a record's page or a search result, newest at the top, and reopening something moves it back to the top instead of duplicating it; it keeps up to ten entries per type and eighty in all, and the panel shows twelve.
It is stored in this device's browser, for this workspace: it does not follow you from computer to phone, it disappears if you clear the site's data, and it is shared with anyone using the same browser profile. 'Clear' empties it, and on a group tab it clears only that group. Below a certain width the button is not there: on a phone the search remains.

leads.title: Leads
leads.subtitle: Managing prospective customers
leads.description: Leads are prospective customers who have shown interest but have not yet been qualified. Every lead has an automatic score (Lead Score) and can be converted into a contact, a company and a sales opportunity.

t01.q: How do I create a new lead?
t01.a: Go to Leads → click the 'New Lead' button at the top right. Fill in first name, last name, email, company and acquisition source (referral, organic, event…). Additional custom fields (if configured by an admin) appear in the same form.

t02.q: What does the Cold / Warm / Hot / Very Hot badge mean?
t02.a: It is the Lead Score, calculated automatically by the system from profile completeness, progress status, recorded interactions and demographic data. Cold (0-25) = low interest; Warm (26-50) = worth nurturing; Hot (51-75) = high priority; Very Hot (76-100) = contact immediately.

t03.q: How do I convert a lead into a contact?
t03.a: Open the lead's profile → click 'Convert Lead'. The system automatically creates: a Contact with all the lead's data, a new Company (if it does not already exist), and a Deal in the pipeline. The original lead is marked as converted and keeps references to the records created.

t04.q: Can I import leads from an Excel or CSV file?
t04.a: Yes. In the Leads list you will find the 'Import CSV' button. Prepare the file with the required columns (first name, last name, email, etc.), upload it and the system will import the records, skipping duplicates automatically (same email = update of the existing record).

t05.q: How do I use filters and saved filters?
t05.a: At the top of the Leads list you will find the filter panel: you can filter by status, source, score, owner, tag and creation date. Once set, click 'Save filter' to reuse it later. Filters can be private or shared with the team. Pinned filters always appear at the top of the list.

t06.a: Select several leads with the checkboxes on the left, then use the bulk actions bar that appears at the bottom: you can delete in bulk, change the status of all selected leads, or reassign the owner in a single operation.

contacts.title: Contacts
contacts.subtitle: Qualified individuals
contacts.description: Contacts are people with whom you have already established, or are establishing, a business relationship. Unlike leads, they are qualified records, often linked to a company and to active deals.

t01.q: What can I record in a contact's profile?
t01.a: Full personal details (first name, last name, job title, department), all contact details (email, phone, mobile, LinkedIn), an address with structured geographic selection, free-form notes and custom tags. You can also record marketing consent (GDPR) with its date.

t02.q: How do I link a contact to a company?
t02.a: In the contact form, use the 'Company' field: search among existing companies or create a new one on the spot. Once linked, the contact also appears in the company's profile, in the 'Associated contacts' section.

t03.q: What will I find on a contact's detail page?
t03.a: The contact's full profile, the linked active deals, the activity timeline (notes, calls, meetings, logged emails), related tasks and custom fields. You can add new activities or tasks directly from this page without leaving the profile.

t04.q: How do I export the contact list?
t04.a: Contacts → 'Export CSV', into a file that Excel and Google Sheets open directly. ⚠️ The export does NOT take the on-screen filter into account: it downloads every contact you are allowed to see. With the admin or owner role that means all of them in the workspace; with other roles only those you own.

t05.q: How do I merge two duplicate contacts?
t05.a: From the list, select the duplicate and use 'Merge': choose which record keeps the field when the two disagree, and everything attached to the duplicate — activities, tasks, deals, tickets — moves to the record that remains, instead of disappearing with it. The same applies to companies and leads.

companies.title: Companies
companies.subtitle: Customer and prospect organisations
companies.description: Companies represent the organisations you work with. They act as the hub that ties together the contacts, deals, activities and tickets of the same business customer.

t01.q: What types of company are there?
t01.a: Prospect (potential customer, not yet active), Customer (active customer), Partner (business partner), Vendor (supplier). The type is shown as a badge in the profile and in the list, and helps you filter your company base quickly.

t02.q: Where do I enter the VAT number and SDI code?
t02.a: The company form has specific fields for Italian tax data: VAT number (Partita IVA) and SDI code (or recipient code for e-invoicing). This data is also available when generating quotes.

t03.q: What will I see on a company's detail page?
t03.a: All company data, linked contacts, open and closed deals, logged activities, open support tickets and notes. Each section has a direct link to add new items without leaving the page.

pipeline.title: Sales Pipeline
pipeline.subtitle: Sales opportunities and deals
pipeline.description: The Pipeline is the heart of the sales process. It shows all open deals organised by stage in a kanban view. Drag the cards to move a deal between stages.

t01.q: How do I create a new deal?
t01.a: From the Pipeline Board click '+ New Deal' (at the top of any column) or use the side menu. Enter name, amount, probability of closing, expected date, company and contact. The deal automatically starts in the first configured stage.

t02.q: How do I analyse leads and deals by territory?
t02.a: First an administrator defines territories in Settings → Territories: by country, by region or province, by postcode prefix, or a combination of the three. For Italy, the abbreviation, name or region all count, so a 'Lombardia' territory includes records written as 'MI', 'Milano' or 'Bergamo'; next to each entry the screen says how it reads it and flags the ones it does not recognise, which helps catch typos. If two territories overlap, the narrower one wins: a postcode beats a province, which beats a country. The report is under Pipeline → By territory: open, new and converted leads, open deals, pipeline, won deals and win rate, over the last 30, 90 or 365 days. A deal is placed by the company's address or, if missing, the contact's. Records no territory covers remain visible in the 'No territory' row. The territory is recalculated from the address every time, so a change to territories applies immediately to existing records too. Territories do not restrict who can see records.

t03.q: How do I move a deal between stages?
t03.a: Drag and drop the deal card into the column of the stage you want. The change is immediate and the system automatically records the stage change in the deal's timeline.

t04.q: What does the Health Score mean?
t04.a: The Health Score (from 0 to 100) indicates the 'health' of the deal: a low score signals that the deal is stagnant, recent activities are missing or the close date has passed. It helps identify the opportunities that need attention.

t05.q: What is the weighted pipeline value?
t05.a: The weighted value is the expected revenue, calculated as: deal amount × probability of closing. For example, a €10,000 deal with a 70% probability contributes €7,000 to the forecast. The Finance Dashboard shows the weighted total as a forecasting indicator.

t06.q: How do I use comments on a deal?
t06.a: Open the deal detail → go to the 'Comments' section. You can leave messages for the team, mention colleagues and reply to existing comments. It is an internal collaboration space for the single opportunity, separate from the activity timeline.

t07.q: Can I get minutes of a meeting?
t07.a: Yes, from the 'Minutes' button above the deal's history, if at least one meeting or call has been logged on that deal. The minutes gather what was written down: the date and duration of each session, who attended, the notes exactly as you wrote them, and, as agreed actions, the tasks created in that window. They invent nothing — this product does not record what is said, so every sentence in the minutes was written by a person. If no task was created they say so, rather than making it look as if the meeting decided nothing. There is a button to copy them.

t08.q: Can I configure my own custom stages?
t08.a: Yes, but only admins can. Go to Settings → Pipeline Stages: you can add, rename, reorder and colour stages. You can also set a default probability of closing for each stage (e.g. 'Proposal sent' = 60%).

finance.title: Finance
finance.subtitle: Financial dashboard and revenue
finance.description: The Finance Dashboard brings together the organisation's actual financial data: revenue from won deals, completed orders and accepted quotes, with a 12-month trend and a weighted pipeline forecast.

t01.q: What is 'actual revenue' in Finance?
t01.a: Actual revenue is calculated by adding up: the values of deals marked as 'Won', the amounts of orders with status 'Completed' and quotes with status 'Accepted'. It does not include deals that are still open or pending quotes.

t02.q: How do I read the 12-month trend chart?
t02.a: The chart shows month by month the revenue realised over the last 12 months. You can compare seasonal patterns, identify the best months and those in decline, and use this data to plan future activities.

t03.q: Does the platform support multiple currencies?
t03.a: Yes. Deals and quotes can be in different currencies (EUR, USD, GBP, etc.). From the dashboard header you can choose the display currency: exchange rates are updated automatically by the system.

products.title: Products
products.subtitle: Catalogue of goods and services
products.description: The Product Catalogue is the central register of all the goods and services your organisation sells. Products are reused in quotes and orders, keeping prices and descriptions consistent.

t01.q: How do I add a product to the catalogue?
t01.a: Go to Products → 'New Product'. Enter name, SKU (product code), unit price, VAT rate, unit of measure and category. The product is immediately available for selection in quotes and orders.

t02.q: What happens if I change the price of a product already used in a quote?
t02.a: Nothing changes in existing quotes. The price is copied into the quote when the line is created ('historical price'), so documents already sent stay unchanged. Only new quotes will use the updated price.

t03.q: How do I deactivate a product I no longer sell?
t03.a: Instead of deleting it (which would break the references in historical documents), use the 'Active/Inactive' toggle. Inactive products do not appear in the selection when creating new quotes, but remain visible in historical documents.

t04.q: What is a price list for?
t04.a: A price list says what a group of customers pays, instead of the catalogue price. You define it in Sales → Price lists in two ways, which work together: a percentage adjustment on the base price (say -10% for resellers, +5% for a channel with a different margin) and, where it matters, the exact price of individual products, which beats the percentage. The list is assigned on the company record: from then on, when you write a quote, an order or an invoice for that customer, the price proposed when you pick a product is the one from their list.

t05.q: If I change a price list, do documents already written change too?
t05.a: No. Quotes, orders and invoices keep the prices they were written with: a list changed today does not rewrite a quote sent last month. Even in the document you are filling in, changing the customer or the list leaves the lines you have already added as they are: a price you typed by hand is never overwritten unless you ask for it.

t06.q: What happens if I delete a list, or a customer has none?
t06.a: A customer with no price list pays the catalogue price. If you delete a list, the customers who were on it are left without one, so they go back to catalogue prices, and documents already written do not change. Mind the sign of the adjustment: it is the direction of the change, not a discount, so -10 means ten per cent less and +10 ten per cent more.

quotes.title: Quotes
quotes.subtitle: Sales proposals and approvals
quotes.description: The Quotes module manages the whole proposal process: from internal drafting with an approval workflow, to sending it by email to the customer with a viewing link, through to acceptance or rejection.

t01.q: How do I create a new quote?
t01.a: Go to Quotes → 'New Quote'. Select the company, the contact and the linked deal. Add product/service lines from the catalogue (or enter free-form data), set any discounts, VAT and the expiry date. The system automatically calculates subtotal, discounts, VAT and final total.

t02.q: What is the approval workflow?
t02.a: It is an optional step, not a block. From a draft you can click 'Request Approval' and the quote moves to 'Pending approval': it is seen by whoever has the workspace admin or owner role, who can approve or reject it with a note. Once approved, the send button appears. Anyone with permission to write quotes can, however, send directly from the draft without going through this: approval is for those who want an internal review, it does not prevent sending for those who do not use it.

t03.q: How do I send the quote to the customer?
t03.a: The send button appears on a draft and on an approved quote. The system prepares an email with a unique link to the quote: the customer opens it without signing in and sees the formatted document. Subject and text can be edited before it goes out, and nothing is sent until you send it.

t04.q: How does the customer see the quote?
t04.a: The customer receives an email with a personal link. Clicking it opens a public page with all the quote details: items, prices, discounts, totals and notes. From the same page they can accept or reject the quote (with the option of leaving a reason if they reject it).

t05.q: How do I know whether the customer has opened the quote?
t05.a: As soon as the customer opens the link, the quote status automatically changes from 'Sent' to 'Viewed' and the exact time it was opened is recorded. You will see this information in the quote's timeline and detail.

t06.q: How do I chase a quote that got no reply?
t06.a: On the quote detail a panel appears on its own when there is a reason to follow up, and says which: never opened, opened but no reply, about to expire, or already expired. These are four different situations and they suggest four different messages — someone who has not opened it is asked whether the email arrived, not for a decision. The panel does not appear on a quote already accepted or rejected, nor on one sent yesterday. The text is a draft: edit it as you like, and it only goes out when you press send.

t07.q: Can I export the quote as a PDF?
t07.a: Yes. On the quote detail you will find the 'Export PDF' button to download the formatted document, ready to send through other channels or to archive.

orders.title: Orders
orders.subtitle: Confirmed sales
orders.description: Orders represent confirmed sales transactions. They are typically generated by converting an accepted quote, but can also be created manually.

t01.q: What statuses does an order have?
t01.a: Draft (order just created, not yet in progress), In progress (being fulfilled), Completed (delivered and closed), Cancelled (revoked). Only 'Completed' orders count towards actual revenue in the Finance Dashboard.

t02.q: How do I see an order's lines?
t02.a: Open the order detail: you will find all products with quantity, unit price and line total, and the total at the bottom. The creation and order dates also show the exact time, not just the day.

t03.q: How do I move an order forward?
t03.a: Next to the status menu there are two separate buttons, each with its own icon: one moves the order to the next step of the flow (draft → in progress → completed), the other marks it completed in one go. They are kept apart on purpose, because they are two different intentions and mixing them up is costly: an order closed by mistake has to be reopened by hand. Neither appears on a completed or cancelled order, because there is nowhere further to go from there.

t04.q: Where do I record payments and delivery?
t04.a: In the order detail you will find the payments panel: payments are listed one by one with date and amount, not added up into a single number, so you can see a deposit followed by a balance. Next to it you can record the actual delivery date.

invoicing.title: Electronic invoicing
invoicing.subtitle: Invoices, credit notes and stamp duty
invoicing.description: The Invoices module issues Italian electronic invoices in FatturaPA format: numbering per series and year, stamp duty worked out from the VAT Natura of the lines, credit notes, and an archive of the XML and the courtesy PDF. Flux produces the file; transmitting it to SDI stays with the channel you already use.

t01.q: What do I have to fill in before issuing my first invoice?
t01.a:
On your side: Settings → E-invoicing, which needs the company name, VAT number, tax regime (RF01 ordinary, RF19 flat-rate, and the others the format allows) and the registered office — street, postcode, town, province, country. The REA details are optional, but all or nothing: office, number and liquidation status together, because SDI rejects half a block. IBAN, bank, email and phone appear on the invoice if you fill them in. A panel at the top of the page says whether the profile is ready and what is missing or malformed.
On the customer's side, in the company's Billing tab: VAT number or tax code, the full address, and an electronic address — an SDI recipient code or a PEC. Without these an invoice can be written but not issued, and the draft says so.

t02.q: How do I issue an electronic invoice?
t02.a:
Sales → Invoices → 'New invoice': on a single page you choose the customer, optionally an order to copy lines and discount from, and fill in lines, payment and due date. From an order's page, the 'Invoice' button opens the same screen already filled in. On lines with 0% VAT the Natura is mandatory, and on lines with VAT it must not be there: those are the two mistakes SDI rejects. A panel lists what is missing before you can issue.
'Issue' assigns the number, sets today's date and freezes the issuer, customer and line data. From then on the invoice cannot be edited or deleted: it is corrected with a credit note. A draft has no number, so deleting one leaves no gaps in the numbering.

t03.q: How do numbering and series work?
t03.a:
The number is not typed in: it is assigned at the moment of issue, from the counter for the invoice's series and year. The series is a short code of letters and digits you choose on the draft; leave it empty and you use the main numbering, where the number reads '12', otherwise '12/B'. Each series has its own counter and starts again at 1 every new year.
The number is taken in the same operation that issues the invoice, so two people pressing 'Issue' together cannot get the same number and a failed attempt uses none: the numbering has no gaps, as the law requires. A number is never reused and an issued invoice is never renumbered.

t04.q: Does Flux send the invoice to SDI?
t04.a: No, not yet, and it is the most important thing to know before you start. Flux builds the XML file, validates it and keeps it; transmission to the Sistema di Interscambio and the receipts that come back — delivered, rejected, not delivered, outcome — have not been built, because the channel to transmit through has not been chosen. In practice: you download the XML from Flux and send it through the intermediary or portal you already use, and follow the outcomes there. So 'Issued' in Flux means the document has been numbered and frozen, not that it has reached the customer.

t05.q: Where do I find the invoice XML file?
t05.a: On the issued invoice, with the 'XML FatturaPA' button. The file is in FatturaPA FPR12 format (schema 1.2.3, specifications 1.4), with the name SDI expects, and is built from the data frozen at the time of issue: downloading it a year from now gives you the same file, even if your company's or the customer's data has changed in the meantime. Every file produced is validated against the official schema of the Agenzia delle Entrate before it leaves.

t06.q: How do I send the invoice to the customer, and where is it archived?
t06.a:
On the issued invoice you will find 'Courtesy PDF', 'XML FatturaPA' and 'Send to customer'. The PDF is a readable copy built from the same data as the XML, with a footer stating that it has no tax value: the real invoice is the XML file transmitted through SDI, and the customer finds it in their reserved area on the Agenzia delle Entrate website. 'Send to customer' sends the PDF as an attachment from the address configured in Settings → Email, suggesting the company's main email; the invoice records when and to whom it was sent.
Right after issue, the XML and PDF are saved in the document archive, with a fingerprint that makes it possible to detect if a file is altered: in that case it is not served, and the document is rebuilt from the frozen data. If archiving failed, the invoice says so and the 'Archive now' button retries it; it also happens on its own at the first download. Note: the Flux archive does not replace legally compliant digital preservation (conservazione sostitutiva), which remains the responsibility of the preservation service you use.

t07.q: How do I correct or cancel an issued invoice?
t07.a:
With a credit note: an issued invoice cannot be edited or deleted. On the invoice press 'Credit note' and choose 'Full reversal', which copies all the lines and is issued as it is, or 'Partial reversal', which starts from the same lines for you to reduce or remove. A TD04 draft is created, linked to the invoice, with the same numbering series, so numbering continues; change it in the draft if you use a series dedicated to credit notes.
On issue the amount is deducted from the invoice's remaining balance, and you cannot reverse more than was invoiced: if two notes are issued at the same time, the second is rejected without using up numbers. On the invoice a panel shows invoiced, reversed and remaining amounts, and the list shows 'Reversed' or 'Partially reversed'. A credit note never charges stamp duty again: the recharge line would give the customer back the €2, while stamp duty already paid is not refunded. Stamp duty on the note itself is decided as for invoices, from the VAT Natura of its lines.

t08.a:
Automatically, from the VAT Natura of each line. Stamp duty of €2.00 is due when the VAT-free lines that require it together exceed €77.47: what counts is their sum, not the invoice total, after the document discount. Exports (N3.1), intra-EU supplies (N3.2), supplies to San Marino (N3.3) and transactions treated as exports (N3.4) are exempt. Note: transactions under a declaration of intent (N3.5) are not exempt, even though they are non-taxable like exports. The margin scheme (N5) pays no stamp duty because VAT is included in the price.
The draft shows whether stamp duty is due and why. You can force it or remove it for special cases, such as a customer's personal exemption, but only by writing the reason, which stays on the invoice. In Settings → E-invoicing you choose whether to charge it to the customer: in that case the invoice gets a line 'Imposta di bollo assolta in modo virtuale' of €2.00 excluding VAT (N1), which does not count towards the threshold.

t09.q: What is the quarterly stamp duty summary for?
t09.a: For knowing how much to pay and when. On the Invoices page a panel estimates the stamp duty for each quarter of the year, counting the issued invoices that carry it, and for each gives the F24 tax code (2521, 2522, 2523, 2524) and the due date, applying the deferrals that apply when the amount stays below €5,000. It is an estimate made from your own data, not a statement from the tax authority: the amount to pay remains the one the Agenzia delle Entrate publishes in the reserved area, and Flux neither prepares nor files the F24.

t10.q: In which language and currency do my customers receive documents?
t10.a:
In the language set on the company record, under 'Document language' (Billing tab): Italian or English. If you leave it on 'Automatic', it is Italian for an address in Italy or with no country, and English for all others. The language applies to the quote PDF and printout, the page the customer opens from the link, the email you send it with and the courtesy copy of the invoice, whatever language you use Flux in: a quote for a German customer goes out in English even if your system is in Italian. An invoice freezes the language at issue, so a copy reprinted next year does not change language along with the customer record.
Amounts are always in the document's currency, chosen when you create the quote, order, contract or invoice, and are never converted: the currency selector in the header only changes the overall dashboard totals. The name at the top of your documents is the company name in Settings → E-invoicing, or the workspace name if you have not filled it in yet.

contracts.title: Contracts and renewals
contracts.subtitle: Recurring agreements and deadlines
contracts.description: In Sales → Contracts you record the agreements that repeat: an amount per period, a term, a notice period. Flux works out on its own where each contract stands, warns the owner before the deadline to decide, and adds up what they are worth in a month.

t01.q: How do I record a recurring contract?
t01.a: Sales → Contracts → 'New contract'. You need a title, the company and, if you want, the contact it goes through and the deal it came from; then the amount with its currency and the billing period — monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or yearly — the start date, the end of the period, the days of notice and, where applicable, automatic renewal with the length of each renewal. The end of the period can be left empty: that is a contract with no expiry. The owner is the person who will get the renewal warning, so it is worth choosing one rather than leaving whoever created the record.

t02.q: What do a contract's statuses mean?
t02.a:
Almost all of them are calculated from the dates, not chosen: 'Not started yet' before the start date, 'Active' while it runs, 'Decision due' as the deadline to renew or cancel approaches, 'Expired' once the period is over. A contract with no end date stays 'Active'. Only the two things that depend on a person are set by hand: 'Draft', until the agreement is closed, and 'Cancelled'.
That is deliberate: a stored status would be wrong from the first morning nobody touched the record, and a renewals list built on it would miss exactly the contracts nobody is looking after. For a customer who cancels use 'Cancelled' rather than deleting: the contract stays in the history.

t03.q: How do the notice period and the reminder work?
t03.a: The deadline to decide is the end of the period minus the days of notice. The contract moves to 'Decision due' a month before that deadline, so there is still time to renew or cancel, and at that point the owner gets a notification in the bell — and a push too, if they have notifications on: 'A contract of mine reaches its notice period' is one of the types that are on by default. The warning comes from a check that runs once a day, so it arrives during the day rather than at an exact moment, and it goes out once per period even though the contract stays 'Decision due' for weeks. The next period of a self-renewing contract gets its own.

t04.q: How does automatic renewal work?
t04.a: A contract with automatic renewal never expires: when the period ends the expiry moves forward on its own by the length you set, and the notice warning repeats before every renewal. Only the date arithmetic moves: renewal does not issue an invoice, does not create an order and does not change the amount — those stay things to do. If the customer cancels, you set 'Cancelled' and the contract stops renewing and stops counting towards recurring revenue.

t05.a: What the contracts earning today are worth in a month. Each amount is brought back to a month — a yearly one divided by twelve, a quarterly one by three — and added up. Only contracts that have started and have not ended count, so neither a draft, nor a signed contract starting next month, nor an expired or cancelled one: counting those would turn a forecast into a fact. You will find it at the top of the Contracts page and on the dashboard, next to the number of contracts waiting for a decision. Contracts written in different currencies give separate figures, one per currency, never a single sum.

targetsFunnel.title: Sales Targets and Funnel
targetsFunnel.subtitle: Goals and sales process analysis
targetsFunnel.description: Planning and analysis tools: Sales Targets let you set sales goals for each salesperson and track progress in real time. The Funnel analyses how effective the conversion process is.

t01.q: How do I set a sales target?
t01.a: Go to Sales Targets → 'New Target'. Select the salesperson, the period (monthly, quarterly or yearly) and the target amount. You can also set a minimum number of deals to close. Admins see everyone's targets; each user sees their own.

t02.q: How do I track progress towards the target?
t02.a: The Target card on the CRM Dashboard shows in real time the progress bar with the percentage achieved against the current month's goal. The actual value is calculated by adding up the deals the salesperson won in the period.

t03.q: What does the Sales Funnel show?
t03.a: The funnel chart shows how many leads/deals move from one stage of the process to the next: prospecting → qualification → proposal → negotiation → closing. The conversion rates between stages show you where the sales process loses the most opportunities.

marketing.title: Marketing
marketing.subtitle: Email templates and campaigns
marketing.description: The Marketing module manages bulk communications to leads and contacts. Create reusable templates with personalisation variables, then launch email campaigns with open and click tracking.

t01.q: How do follow-up sequences work?
t01.a: In Marketing → Sequences you create a series of automatic emails for leads or for contacts: each step says after how many days it goes out, the subject and the text, which you can load from a template and personalise with placeholders. Enrol a person from their record with the 'Sequence' button, or with an automation rule ('Enroll in Sequence'), for example on every new lead. The sequence stops on its own when the person replies, unsubscribes, when the address bounces or changes, when the lead is converted or deleted; you can also stop it by hand. Whoever follows the record receives a notification, including push, when the person replies. Every email has an unsubscribe link, added at the bottom if you do not include it. A person cannot be enrolled twice in the same running sequence. A paused sequence sends nothing and enrolled people stay where they are. Note: replies are detected only if inbound email is configured; if it is not, the Sequences page says so.

t02.q: How do I create an email template?
t02.a: Marketing → Templates → 'New Template'. Give it a name, write subject and body in HTML, and use placeholders to personalise each copy: first name, last name, full name, company, email, phone and job title, each between double curly braces. The same ones also work in English (first_name, last_name, company…) and with a few synonyms — societa counts as azienda — because a placeholder written almost right must not go out to the customer as it is. Spaces inside the braces are tolerated. There is also a placeholder for the unsubscribe link, which must be included in every campaign.

t03.q: How do I create and send a campaign?
t03.a: Go to Marketing → Campaigns → 'New Campaign'. Choose the template, select the recipients (contacts with marketing consent or leads), then click 'Send Now' or schedule sending for a future date/time. The system queues the sending, with automatic retry on temporary errors.

t04.q: How does email tracking work?
t04.a: The system automatically detects when a recipient opens the email (through a tracking pixel) and when they click a link. In the campaign report you will find: number of emails sent, opened, clicked, bounced and unsubscribes, with percentages (open rate, click-through rate).

t05.q: What happens if a contact unsubscribes?
t05.a: The address goes onto the suppression list and is excluded from every subsequent send, even if someone adds it back to the recipients by hand. ⚠️ The list works on the ADDRESS, not on the record: ticking marketing consent on the contact again does not bring them back among the recipients, because these are two different things — consent says what you would like to do, suppression says what the person asked for. Hard bounces and spam complaints end up there too, by the same route.

tasks.title: Tasks and Projects
tasks.subtitle: Task management, Gantt and workload
tasks.description: The Tasks module is a project management system built into the CRM. Tasks can stand alone or be linked to leads, contacts, companies, deals or tickets. It supports subtask hierarchies, multiple assignees and dependencies.

t01.q: How do I create a task?
t01.a: Go to Tasks → 'New Task'. Enter title, description, due date, priority (low, normal, high, critical, blocker) and assign the task to a colleague. You can link it to a CRM record (lead, company, deal) so it is easy to find from that record's profile too.

t02.q: What are subtasks?
t02.a: A task can contain subtasks (up to 3 levels deep). This lets you break complex work down into smaller steps. The parent task's progress percentage is calculated automatically from the completion of its children.

t03.q: Can I assign a task to more than one person?
t03.a: Yes. Every task supports multiple assignees with distinct roles: Responsible (does the work), Accountable (holds responsibility), Consulted (provides input), Informed (is kept updated on progress). You can add all the members you need.

t04.q: How does the Gantt chart work?
t04.a: The Gantt view (Tasks → Gantt) shows tasks on a horizontal timeline. Each bar represents a task's duration. You can drag the bars to change dates, see the hierarchy (task → subtask) and set dependencies between tasks (e.g. 'task B starts only after task A is completed').

t05.a: The Workload view (Tasks → Workload) shows, for each team member, how many hours of work are planned week by week. Red cells signal overload; grey ones indicate under-use. Useful for balancing the load across people.

t06.q: I can no longer find a task I completed months ago. Where has it gone?
t06.a: The task list is a work queue, not an archive: it always shows everything that is still open, whatever the date, plus only what was completed in the last 30 days. When something is left out, a line above the list says how many tasks are hidden, with a 'Show them' link to see them all. Nothing is deleted, and a direct link to a task still opens it, however old it is.

t07.q: The list says it shows only the first 500 tasks. Why?
t07.a: It is a safety limit: beyond that number the page would become slow for everyone, including someone looking for a single task. When the limit kicks in the list says so, instead of stopping silently. Use the filters at the top — status, priority, assignee — or search to narrow down and find what you are looking for.

t08.q: How do I log time worked on a task?
t08.a: In the task detail you will find the 'Time Tracking' section. Start the timer when you begin working and stop it when you finish, or enter the hours manually. The system compares estimated and actual hours, giving you a view of how well planned times are being kept.

calendar.title: Calendar and Appointments
calendar.subtitle: Managing meetings and availability
calendar.description: The Calendar brings together all the team's appointments. It supports in-person and virtual meetings (Zoom, Teams, Jitsi), invitations with RSVP and direct links to CRM records.

t01.q: How do I create an appointment?
t01.a: In the Calendar click a free time slot or the 'New Appointment' button. Enter title, start and end date/time, time zone, physical location or virtual meeting link (Zoom, Teams, Jitsi or other). You can link the appointment to a contact, company, lead or deal.

t02.q: How do I invite participants?
t02.a: In the appointment form you will find the 'Participants' section. Add internal colleagues or external contacts with their role (Required, Optional). Each participant receives a notification and can reply Accept / Decline / Maybe directly from the invitation email, without having to sign in.

t03.q: Can I see these appointments in my personal calendar?
t03.a:
Yes, in both directions, from the 'Subscribe' button at the top of the Calendar page.

FROM HERE TO YOUR CALENDAR: the window gives you an address to paste into Google Calendar, Outlook or Apple Calendar, and from then on the appointments scheduled here appear there and keep themselves up to date. ⚠️ That address works like a password: a calendar program cannot sign in, so the address is what says who you are, and anyone who receives it can read your appointments.

FROM YOUR CALENDAR TO HERE: in the same window you paste your calendar's secret iCal address — in Google it is under Settings → your calendar → Secret address in iCal format — and its appointments appear here as busy time, in grey, so nobody books something else on top of them. They are not records: they cannot be opened or edited.

The two directions are independent and each works on its own. If an event in your calendar uses a recurrence we cannot expand, you are told instead of it being hidden: a week that looks free because something was not read is worse than a warning.

t04.q: Does the Dashboard also show today's appointments?
t04.a: Yes. The Agenda widget on the CRM Dashboard shows in real time all your commitments for today: tasks falling due, planned activities (calls, meetings) and appointments. Events are sorted chronologically.

chat.title: Internal Chat
chat.subtitle: Messaging between colleagues
chat.description: The Chat module lets team members talk to each other directly without leaving the platform. It supports 1:1 direct messages and group conversations.

t01.q: How do I start a chat with a colleague?
t01.a: Go to Chat → 'New Conversation' → search for the colleague's name. You can start a private 1:1 chat or create a group (a named multi-user chat). Conversations remain available after the session ends.

t02.q: Can I mute a conversation?
t02.a: Yes. From any conversation, use the 'Mute' option and choose for how long: the conversation keeps receiving messages, but will not send you notifications until the mute expires.

tickets.title: Support Tickets
tickets.subtitle: Customer support management
tickets.description: The Tickets module manages customer support requests in an omnichannel system. Tickets collect communications from email, chat, phone and social media, with configurable SLAs and a full audit log.

t01.q: How do I create a new ticket?
t01.a: Go to Tickets → 'New Ticket'. Enter subject, description, source channel (email, chat, phone, social), priority and type (support, bug, complaint, information request, internal task). Link the ticket to an existing contact, company or lead.

t02.q: What statuses does a ticket have?
t02.a: New (just opened), Open (taken on), In progress (an agent is working on it), Pending (waiting for the customer's reply), On hold, Resolved (solution provided, awaiting confirmation), Closed (definitively concluded). Moving a ticket to 'Pending' pauses the SLA timer.

t03.q: What are SLAs?
t03.a: SLAs define the maximum first response and resolution times for each priority. For example: urgent ticket → first response within 1 hour, resolution within 4 hours. They do not wait for the breach to tell you: they warn at 50% and at 80% of the time elapsed, measured on the individual ticket's window, so a four-hour policy and a two-day policy warn at the same point in their own terms. On breach, if the policy names a group, the alert goes to everyone in that group as well as to whoever is handling the ticket.

t04.q: Do SLAs keep counting at night and at weekends?
t04.a: It depends on the individual policy. By default they count on wall-clock time: a four-hour promise on a ticket that arrived on Friday at 17:00 expires at 21:00 on Friday, when nobody is there. Turning on 'Business hours' for that policy stops the count outside opening hours, on closing days and holidays, and resumes it when you open. The setting is per policy and starts off: quietly changing the meaning of a promise already made would be a surprise, not a fix. The working week, time zone and closing days are set on the SLA page.

t05.q: Does the ticket tell me where it stands and what it resembles?
t05.a: Yes, in two separate panels at the top of the right-hand column. The first says whose move it is — whether it is waiting on us or on the customer — and for how long, measured from the last message rather than from when it was opened, then quotes the initial question in the customer's own words and the latest internal note, that is, what has already been tried. If nobody has replied yet it says so plainly: an internal note does not count as a reply. The second shows what the ticket resembles among those this workspace has already resolved, with a suggested category and priority and the tickets they come from, which you can click: so you can see why and disagree. None of this is applied automatically, and when the similar tickets do not agree the panel prefers to suggest nothing.

t06.a: Macros are predefined replies to the most frequent questions: instead of writing the same thing again, you pick one and the text goes into the reply box, ready to edit. Placeholders such as the ticket number, the customer's name and yours are filled in when it is inserted. You can choose them from the 'Macro' menu above the reply box, or press directly the ones the suggestions panel proposes for this ticket.

t07.q: How does the ticket Kanban work?
t07.a: The Kanban view shows tickets organised by status in side-by-side columns. You can drag a ticket from one column to another to change its status. Each card shows: ticket number, priority, assignee and last update time.

t08.q: Can I leave internal notes on a ticket?
t08.a: Yes. In the ticket thread you can choose whether the message is 'Public' (visible to the customer) or 'Internal' (visible only to the team). Internal notes have a different background so they are easy to tell apart from replies to the customer.

automation.title: Automation
automation.subtitle: Automatic if-then rules
automation.description: The Automation Engine lets you create automatic rules that fire when events happen in the system. It removes repetitive manual work by configuring conditional automatic actions.

t01.q: How do I create an automation rule?
t01.a: Go to Automation → 'New Rule'. Choose: the target record type (deal, lead, contact, company), the trigger (on creation or on update), the conditions (e.g. 'deal amount > 5000'), and the actions to perform. Click 'Save and Activate' to put it live.

t02.q: What actions can a rule perform?
t02.a: Seven: send an email, create a task linked to the record, update a field on the record (for example the status), assign the record in turn to a group of people, send an internal notification to a colleague, call a webhook, and emit an event to a connected integration. The event is marked as originating from a person, not a machine, because the rule fires on something somebody did: otherwise an integration that ignores its own writes would take it for its own and not react.

t03.q: How do I distribute new leads in turn among salespeople?
t03.a: Create a rule on leads, with the 'on creation' trigger, and choose the 'Assign Owner (round robin)' action. Tick the people in the order you want them to receive leads: the first lead goes to the first person, the second to the second, and so on, starting again from the top. Whoever receives the lead is told with a notification. Two leads arriving at the same instant still go to two different people. Anyone who has left the workspace in the meantime is skipped without having to edit the rule, and a lead someone has already taken on stays with that person, unless you tick 'Reassign records that already have an owner'. It also works for contacts, companies and deals.

t04.q: Can I assign leads based on territory or source?
t04.a: Yes, in the same 'Assign Owner (round robin)' action. With 'Add route' you add one or more routes: each specifies one or more territories, one or more sources (for example 'website, trade fair') or both, and the people who take turns on those leads. Routes are tried from top to bottom and the first one that matches decides, so put the most specific cases at the top; use the arrows to change the order. Each route has its own rotation, independent of the others. If all the people in a route have left the workspace, the lead passes to the next route. Leads no route picks up go to the people listed under 'Everyone else'; if nobody is listed there, they stay unassigned. Use a single rule with several routes, not several separate rules: rules run in parallel, and two rules assigning the same lead would compete for the record. A deal is placed by the company's address or, if missing, the contact's.

t05.q: Do I have to write every rule from scratch?
t05.a: No. The Automation page has a library of ready-made rules for the most common situations — a lead to call back, an important deal that has just come in, an urgent ticket, a thank-you to the customer. You pick one, adapt it and activate it: it is faster than starting from a blank page, and it shows how rules are built.

t06.a: Besides equals and not equals: greater than, less than, greater than or equal, less than or equal, contains, does not contain, is empty, is not empty. And three that look at the change rather than the value — has changed, has become, was — which are for reacting to a status transition rather than to the status itself.

t07.a: Example: 'When a deal is created with an amount greater than €10,000, automatically create a task for the sales manager titled High-value deal review, due in 2 days'. Or: 'When a lead is qualified, send a welcome email to the contact and notify the assigned agent'.

t08.q: How do I check that rules are working?
t08.a: On the Automation page you will find the 'Execution log' section: for each run you see the record involved, the outcome (success or error), the actions performed and any error message. If a rule does not fire as expected, check the logs to understand why.

reports.title: Reports and Analytics
reports.subtitle: Performance analysis and custom reports
reports.description: The Reports module provides analysis of operational performance: global KPIs, activity per user, completed tasks and campaigns sent. The Report Builder lets you create custom reports without writing code.

t01.q: What do the standard reports show?
t01.a: The standard reports include: total actions logged in the period (per user or for the whole team), completed tasks, deals created and closed, tickets opened and resolved, email campaigns sent. All data can be filtered by date and by individual user.

t02.q: How do I use the Report Builder?
t02.a: Go to Reports → Report Builder. Select the record type to analyse (deals, contacts, leads, tickets, etc.), choose the metrics to display, apply filters and choose the chart type (bar, line, pie or table). You can save the report to consult it later or share it with the team.

t03.q: Can I export the activity log?
t03.a: Yes, as CSV, filterable by date range and by individual person. It requires the workspace admin role: it is the record of who did what, so it is not a read like any other.

t04.q: Where do I find the advanced pipeline analytics?
t04.a:
Under Sales → Pipeline, and they are four pages answering four different questions. Funnel: where leads drop off along the way. Win/Loss: why deals are won and lost, with the reasons recorded at closing. Forecast: what it is reasonable to expect this month, by owner. Pipeline report: the distribution by stage. Targets sit alongside, under Sales targets.

What needs attention right now — stalled deals, quotes never opened, SLAs close to their deadline — is not on an analytics page but in the next actions panel on the dashboard, where every row opens the record it comes from.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: System configuration (admins only)
settings.description: The Settings section groups all the platform's global configuration. Access is restricted to admins and owners.

t01.q: How do I add custom fields?
t01.a: Settings → Custom Fields. Select the record type (contact, lead, company, deal), choose the field type (text, number, date, select, multi-select, yes/no, URL), give it a name and save. The field appears immediately in the form of every record of that type.

t02.q: How do I configure the email sender?
t02.a: Settings → Email. Choose the provider: Resend (your API key is enough) or SMTP (host, port, credentials and TLS). Then set the sender name and the address everything goes out from: campaigns, invitations, notifications. ⚠️ That address is not only for sending: it is also the one customers reply to, and the one the system uses to recognise that an incoming email belongs to this workspace. If it is left empty, incoming emails do not become tickets.

t03.q: I can no longer find a ticket closed months ago.
t03.a: The ticket list is a work queue: it always shows everything that is still open, in progress or pending, whatever the date, plus only what was resolved or closed in the last 30 days. When something is left out, a line above the status tabs says how many tickets are hidden, with a link to see them all. Nothing is deleted.

t04.q: How do I manage canned replies for tickets?
t04.a: Settings → Macros. Create new macros with a title and pre-filled text. Public macros are visible to the whole team in the tickets module; private ones are visible only to you. They are available directly in the ticket's reply box.

integrations.title: Integrations and API
integrations.subtitle: API key and the assistant's contribution
integrations.description: An external system — a website, a back-office, an assistant — writes into Flux through the /api/crm/* routes, using a workspace key. In Analysis → Assistant's contribution you can see what it wrote.

t01.q: How do I connect an external program to Flux?
t01.a:
Settings → API, where you generate the workspace key. It is sent as the header `Authorization: Bearer <key>` and is valid only for this workspace: the key itself says which one, so whoever integrates does not have to state it anywhere else and cannot hit the wrong workspace by mistake. The same page shows this business's identifier, which is what integration addresses are built from.
There is one key per workspace and you see it once, when it is created: it cannot be read back. If you lose it you create another, and the old one stops working at that same moment — so the integration has to be updated at the same moment. 'Revoke' switches it off immediately without creating a new one. Flux does not record when a key was last used: to see whether an integration is working, look at the Assistant's contribution.

t02.q: What can an API key do?
t02.a:
Write, not read. The routes available are all POST and cover contacts, leads, companies, notes, orders, activities (including activities on a contact, a lead, a company or a deal), custom fields, moving a lead to another stage, closing a person's deals, opting a contact point out, and GDPR erasure. Nearly all of them also have a 'bulk' version for sending several records at once.
⚠️ There is no read route at all: from outside you cannot read back a list of contacts or orders, so reconciling weeks later against what the CRM actually holds is not possible and has to be done from the screens. A key is the equivalent of a user who can write records, not an administrator: it changes no settings. Calls are counted against the workspace's plan, and past the limit the answer is 429.

t03.q: What does a request with several records answer?
t03.a: Always 200, even when some records were rejected. The body holds a summary — total, created, updated, skipped, errors and duration — and a list with one entry per record sent: its position, its outcome, the id it was given, or the field-by-field reasons it was rejected. A bad row does not fail the whole request, so an integrator should not be waiting for an error status: the answer is in the body.

t04.q: How do I repeat a call without duplicating data?
t04.a:
By sending the `Idempotency-Key` header with a value of your own, different for every request. It matters because an answer that never arrives — a timeout, a dropped connection — leaves the caller not knowing whether the work was done, and sending it all again duplicates whatever Flux cannot recognise: contacts and leads are matched on email alone, which is optional, and activities are matched on nothing.
With the key, the first request imports and every identical repeat gets the same answer back, with the same ids, having written nothing, marked `Idempotent-Replay: true`. The same key with a different body is refused with 422, one still in flight with 409, and keys are forgotten after thirty days. With no header nothing changes from how it was. It is accepted by the contacts, leads, companies, notes, orders and activities routes, both single and bulk; it is not accepted yet by the lead stage change, custom fields, closing deals, opt-out and erasure.

t05.q: What does the 'Assistant's contribution' page show?
t05.a:
What came into the CRM from integrations, in the current month: how many records were written, in how many requests, when the last one arrived, and a table by kind — contacts, companies, leads, notes, activities, orders, custom fields, closed deals, withdrawn consents, erasures. It sits under Analysis, not inside Reports, because whoever connects an integration needs to be able to check it whether or not they bought the reporting module.
Three warnings. It counts only writes that arrived through the API routes: what the team does inside Flux does not go through them and does not appear, so this is not a comparison between people and the assistant. One request can write many rows — a five-hundred-contact import is one request and five hundred rows — which is why the two columns are separate. And a key identifies the workspace, not who is using it: with two integrations connected the figures are their sum. Erasures are counted without saying who they were about, so as to leave no trail back to someone who asked to disappear.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.subtitle: Real-time alerts and updates
notifications.description: The bell in the header shows unread alerts while you are in Flux. Push notifications, if you turn them on, reach you even when Flux is closed, just as an installed app would.

t01.q: Which events generate a notification?
t01.a: When a task assigned to you is about to fall due or is overdue, when one of your deals is closed as won, when a lead is assigned to you, when a campaign you started goes out, when a contract you own reaches its notice period, and when somebody replies to a sequence. On quotes: an approval request and the outcome that follows it. On tickets: when an SLA promise has used up half its time and then 80%, so you can still do something about it, and on breach — which also alerts the people in the group named in the policy, each of them only once. On top of that, chat messages, direct messages and mentions in notes. Automations can add more.

t02.q: Can I receive notifications even when Flux is closed?
t02.a: Yes. Go to Settings → Notifications and turn on notifications on this device: the browser asks you for permission once, and from then on alerts arrive like those of an installed app. Permission applies to one browser and one device at a time, so phone and computer have to be turned on separately, and on the same page you see the list of registered devices so you can remove one you no longer use. There is also a button to send yourself a test and check straight away that it works.

t03.q: On iPhone I cannot find the button to turn them on.
t03.a: Apple only delivers notifications to apps added to the home screen, never to a Safari tab. Open the share menu, choose 'Add to Home Screen', then open Flux from the icon: from there the button appears. On Android and on a computer there is nothing to install.

t04.q: I get too many notifications. Can I choose which ones?
t04.a:
Yes, in Settings → Notifications there is a switch for each type of event. Six are on by default, the ones that usually need someone straight away: a lead assigned to you, one of your tasks falling due, a ticket close to its SLA, a ticket that has breached it, a contract you own reaching its notice period, and a reply to a sequence. Everything else — chat and direct messages, mentions in notes, quote approvals and outcomes, won deals — is off until you turn it on.
There is also a main switch that pauses them all without losing your individual choices. Only the choices you actually make are stored, so a type of alert added later arrives at whatever it is meant to be by default instead of being silently off. The bell inside Flux keeps showing everything regardless.

t05.q: I said no to the browser and now it does not ask any more.
t05.a: That is normal behaviour: a browser that has been told no does not ask for permission a second time. You need to reopen it from the site settings in the browser — usually from the icon to the left of the address — allow notifications for Flux and reload the page.

t06.q: How do I mark notifications as read?
t06.a: Click the bell icon → the panel with recent notifications opens. Click a notification to go to the corresponding page (the notification is marked as read). Or use 'Mark all as read' to clear them all in one go.

mobileApp.title: The app on your phone
mobileApp.subtitle: Installing and using Flux on mobile
mobileApp.description: Flux can be added to the home screen and opens full screen, with its own icon and no browser bar. Below a certain width the interface changes shape, not just size.

t01.q: How do I install Flux on my phone?
t01.a: Open Flux in the phone's browser and add it to the home screen. On Android and Chrome-based browsers the 'Install' prompt appears, and Flux itself offers it once: dismiss it and it does not come back, but the option stays in the browser menu. On iPhone and iPad there is no button: use Share → 'Add to Home Screen'. Once installed, Flux opens on the dashboard full screen, and holding the icon gives you shortcuts to Pipeline, Tickets and New order.

t02.q: What changes when using Flux on a phone?
t02.a: A bar appears at the bottom with five destinations, chosen from the ones you have access to, while the full menu stays in the button at the top left — the same side its panel comes out of. Long lists (contacts, companies, leads, orders, quotes, tickets) become cards instead of tables: a nine-column table does not become usable by scrolling sideways. Dialogs open full screen, so the keyboard does not end up on top of them. On a computer everything is as it was: these are two layouts of the same screen, not two products.

t03.q: Does Flux work without a connection?
t03.a: No, and that is on purpose. Every page and every figure comes over the network: with no connection you get a screen that says so, instead of the browser's error page. Nothing you see is kept on the phone, because a saved copy does not know which workspace it came from or what role you had when you opened it, and a pipeline from twenty minutes ago is worse than no pipeline — nothing on the screen would say it was old, and somebody would quote from it to a customer. When a new version is released Flux tells you and reloads only when you press, so it does not update while you are writing a quote.

t04.q: Do push notifications work on a phone?
t04.a: Yes, but on iPhone and iPad only if you have added Flux to the home screen: Apple does not deliver them to a Safari tab, and until you install the app the button to turn them on stays disabled with an explanation. On Android and on a computer nothing needs installing. Permission is given once per browser and per device, so a phone and a laptop are turned on separately; it is done in Settings → Notifications, where you also choose which kinds of alert reach you and see the list of registered devices.

usersRoles.title: Users and Roles
usersRoles.subtitle: Access and permission management (admins only)
usersRoles.description: The access management system controls who can do what on the platform. Four hierarchical role levels ensure every user sees and changes only what concerns them.

t01.q: Which roles are available?
t01.a: Owner: full access, including administration of the workspace. Admin: users, roles and settings. Editor: creates and edits CRM records. Viewer: read-only. They are hierarchical — each role includes the permissions of the one below — and they apply WITHIN this workspace: they are a different thing from the role of Flux staff, who operate the administration panel and have nothing to do with what you see here. ⚠️ Read-only means everywhere, including the API: a call made with a viewer's session is refused just as a button would be.

t02.q: How do I invite a new user?
t02.a: Users → 'Invite User'. Enter the new member's email and select the role to assign. The system automatically sends an email with a link to accept the invitation. The link is valid for a limited time and lets the invitee set their own password.

t03.q: How do I change a user's role?
t03.a: Users → find the person in the list → open the role menu and choose a new one. ⚠️ It does not take effect instantly: the role is re-read at most every five minutes, so until then a session already open keeps the previous permissions. The same applies to removal from the workspace. If you need to revoke access immediately, remove the person and have them signed out.

t04.q: What are User Groups?
t04.a: Groups let you organise users into teams (e.g. 'North Sales Team', 'Level 2 Support'). You can assign leads, contacts, companies and deals to a group instead of a single user. Useful for managing visibility and dividing work between teams.
